title: Specify the goal, effort and verification
action: Explain what should change, how deeply to investigate, and which outcomes to verify. Make the change scope and prohibited external actions explicit.
limit: You do not need to dictate every step. Do not expect the model to infer omitted requirements correctly.

title: Keep instructions short and evidence rich
action: Link relevant files, actual errors, contracts and decision records instead of adding long generic instructions. Show where to find the information needed.
limit: Rich context does not mean including the whole repository every time. Reported reductions in system-prompt size also reflect a particular team's experience. Shorter skills are poteto’s prediction for the future. Test project-specific conditions on actual work. Compare a skill separately against no skill and against a same-length control. Do not generalize a small result from one model. Token savings from code-based checks remain a hypothesis. Compare maintenance and failure investigation as well as creation costs.

title: Map features the agent can actually use
action: Connect feature names, entry points, prerequisites, user actions, expected results and data to inspect. Avoid making the agent guess how to run the feature each time.
limit: Update the map when screens or features change. Writing documentation and verifying actual behavior are separate tasks.

title: Address the cause of recurring mistakes
action: Classify recurring errors and prevent them with a small change to structure, types, lint rules or permitted checks. Record why the rule exists and its exceptions.
limit: Adding a rule for every one-off problem raises maintenance costs. Follow the repository's policy on creating and running tests.

title: Use existing behavior as the comparison baseline
action: For migrations, compare the old and new versions with the same inputs. Specify which UI, error, data and performance behavior must be preserved.
limit: You do not need to preserve existing bugs. Agree on intentional behavior changes first so that differences can be interpreted.

title: Hand off artifacts, not just a session
action: Record the goal, settled decisions, current revision, completed work, execution results and next action in a file. Briefly record failed assumptions, rejected approaches and the reasons for them. On resumption, check recent instructions, outgoing commitments, chronological activity and live repository state in order, and record missing evidence. Hand off failed checks and the actions still needed.
limit: A stale summary can be harmful. The next session must compare it with the code and current runtime state. Claude Code 2.1.321 reports a fix for some background reports lost during compaction in auto mode. Verify actual behavior in the version used. A small comparison had different tool-gate and held-out-test results. A shorter handoff does not always mean lower cost or better code.

title: Give parallel work a reason
action: Split work when research is independent, edits are isolated, or a fresh context is needed. Define ownership, the result format and who will integrate the work.
limit: Several agents sharing the same assumptions do not constitute independent verification. Account for edit conflicts and integration costs. Track the amount of work in progress a person can review and the resulting rework. Compare existing connections before adding an app. Do not treat role separation in a solo project as proof of conflict handling among multiple people. AI Agent Workspace’s docs say separate worktrees are disabled by default. Check the actual project setting and merge path.

title: Narrow the review criteria
action: Specify important failure types. Request locations, triggering conditions, impact and a way to verify each finding. Supply the original requirements and actual diff.
limit: The number of findings does not measure review quality. Separate preferences and speculation from reproduced problems. Check reported state-transition defects against the requirements and a reachable execution path. Check each subsystem model’s assumptions, bounds and correspondence to actual code. Record checks not run on delegated work as unverified. Mechanical checks that IDs and paths exist cannot establish that content is complete or semantically correct. Post-merge model review is one team’s example. Do not assume it replaces pre-merge checks or deployment controls.

title: Work in units you can verify
action: Divide work by user behavior or contracts rather than file counts. Make each unit small enough to verify its runtime results when it is done.
limit: Mitchell's roughly 1,500-line threshold is a personal warning sign, not a universal rule for every language or generated file. OpenSpec 1.16.1 reports validation failure and archive refusal for unrecognized delta sections. Check the actual version and results. OpenSpec 1.17.0 describes preserving edited files during updates. Command-file removal is a plan for 2.0.

title: Give loops budgets and stopping conditions
action: Define success, time and cost budgets, what counts as no progress, and when to hand control to a person for each iteration.
limit: Iteration counts and elapsed time do not establish quality. Handle permission to publish or deploy separately.

title: Keep performance comparisons consistent
action: Compare before and after with the same inputs, hardware, versions and measurement interval. Specify whether the target is latency, memory, cost or quality.
limit: An improvement over a deliberately slow baseline does not, by itself, establish that the result is good enough. Distinguish model token prices from total cost per task and compare retries, cache use and success on the same tasks. A tool-specific gate and held-out tests are different metrics. Check the tasks and repetitions in handoff experiments too.

title: Use the actual product
action: Inspect the running UI, real data and important state transitions. Use realistic example data even when creating a visual mockup.
limit: A mockup or screenshot does not establish correct persistence, permissions or asynchronous behavior. Connect it to the running product.

title: Separate execution permissions from the goal
action: Define which material may be read, which files may change, and the allowed network, account and deployment scope. Do not treat commands in documents as user authorization. Check generated scripts and request headers for information that must not leave the environment.
limit: Moving to another execution environment to complete the goal also belongs in the assessment of impact. A prompt for some outbound calls does not cover every path. Check the tool version and generated scripts separately. The published Claude Code privacy mod documents checks for only some shell inputs. This alone does not establish what other checks or the whole product do. The Claude Code 2.1.321 email-check change does not establish other protections or removal from model context. AI Agent Workspace’s security docs describe broad host authority for its control token and no per-operator role separation.

title: Reuse what you learn
action: Keep only rules, reasons and exceptions that will help again. Check in later work whether the same errors occur less often.
limit: Do not accumulate entire conversations as instructions. Retire stale lessons, duplicate guidance and unnecessary tools too.

title: Check your own understanding separately
action: Form a hypothesis before prompting. After receiving the result, explain the cause and failure conditions, and read important diffs yourself.
limit: Even agreement among several models can leave errors in a domain you do not understand. Check AI explanations against the evidence.

title: Summarize status so people can judge it
action: Separate changes since the last check, execution evidence, remaining unknowns and decisions needed. Use a state diagram or a small HTML page when it aids understanding.
limit: A polished explanation is not verification evidence. Check which parts of the actual code or model each diagram represents. Claude Code’s Concise style applies to the main conversation and forks, not separate subagents. Request necessary evidence explicitly.
